document.title: Expected eval outcomes and a skill pass that meets more of them
document.summary: Each eval case gets an `expected.md` and tighter `case.json` gates. The skill adds source-vs-head lookFor, a stricter why, and grouping rules the harness can check. The runner takes model params, names the case work tree, defaults the producer to `grok-4.6:effort=high`, and can `--rescore` saved reviews.
document.why: [#117](source:s1) says the gating checks on main always pass and are too loose to steer the skill. Write a human expected outcome per case, fold it into expects, and iterate the skill until reviews match.

sources.title: [Compre] Manually review eval cases and write expected outcomes
sources.gist: Gating checks on main always pass and are too loose. Write expected outcomes, fold them into case.json, iterate the skill until reviews match across repeated runs.

sources.label: PR #118
sources.title: Expected eval outcomes and a skill pass that meets more of them (#117)
sources.gist: Phase 1 expected outcomes plus a first phase 2 skill pass. Default producer is now grok-4.6 high. Graders stay grok-4.6.

lookFor: [#117](source:s1) is done when the skill meets the new expects across repeated graded runs. This branch's Composer rounds were 30/59. One Grok 4.6 high sample was 10/10. The repeated Grok suite is not in this diff.

groups.summary: The next skill checks each source against head, writes why only from a stated problem or goal, keeps tests and copies with the code they serve, and bullets hidden behavior and overridden ticket items.

groups.why: The runner has to check the new expects and run the stronger producer [#117](source:s1) needs.

lookFor: Subtle: `--rescore` clones a fresh work tree, so a producer that left the tree dirty does not fail again.

commits.subject: Eval: re-score saved reviews with --rescore
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Feed eval/runs/<stamp> review.json files through validate and the deterministic checks. Skip the producer, the graders, and the API key. Use this after editing expects.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Eval: default producer to Grok 4.6 high
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
The producer comparison on this PR showed grok-4.6:effort=high passing every gate in its sample and finding the hard claims Composer missed. Leave the grader on grok-4.6 at default effort.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Eval: name the case work tree in the producer prompt
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Opus 5.5 ran shell commands in the runner's own checkout, found neither ref, and stopped. The prompt now gives the work tree path instead of 'the current directory'.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Eval: accept model params in --producer-model and --grader-model
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
id:param=value,... passes reasoning effort and other variant params to the SDK, e.g. grok-4.6:effort=high.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Keep the canonical schema free to sit with its generator on comprehende-57
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Graded runs put the two identical copies in their own skim-safe group and the canonical file with its generator and drift test, which is a good review. Fix the document lookFor omit rule to cover manual-step bullets.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Skill: why in the source's terms, overridden ticket items, manual steps
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Graders flagged whys that add a reader need no source names, and a group why that cited a ticket for the opposite of its ask. Reviews dropped a ticket item a review comment overrode, and a one-time setup step the PR named.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Skill: bullet unmentioned behavior changes and non-obvious review fixes
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Bulleting only source divergences dropped resolved review comments with non-obvious fixes and behavior changes no source names.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Skill: keep a feature's pieces in one group, and copies with their source
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Runs split a new feature into seed, helper, and spec groups, and moved identical copies into their own mechanical group.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Skill: unasked work gets its own part; order parts a story builds on first
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
The one-part fallback satisfied the dependsOn rule while hiding unasked product events. Leave the why ungated on vitadeck-24 and comprehende-67: their whys restate the PR, and the prose grader already flags invented ones. Allow 3 parts on cigster-99 (one harness part) and 5 groups on comprehende-59, and note that the living-room spec builds on the page objects.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Skill: find the source sentence for the why, and check placement before done
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
The why needs a source sentence that states a problem or goal; a sentence that only says what changes goes in the summary. Step 5 is not done until tests, one-line call sites, and dependsOn sit where the grouping rules put them. vitadeck-24 and comprehende-67 now expect no why: their PRs say what changes but state no problem or goal.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Eval: gate group count and cross-part dependsOn
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Add a groups { min, max } expect and a check that fails when a group depends on a group in another part. Set a groups range on every case from its expected.md. Replace the comprehende-57 and comprehende-59 triples with test-with-code pairs: they asked to fold a foundation into its call site, which the skill allows. Allow a second part for the vitadeck-24 CI step.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Skill: check sources against head and group by concern
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Give every source item a verdict from the code at head and bullet only divergences. Take the why from a stated problem or goal. Keep tests, one-line call sites, and re-exports in the group they serve, keep dependsOn inside a part, make unasked work its own part, and have mechanical summaries say what the reader can skip.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Expect no document why on comprehende-59
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Its ticket, #58, is not linked from the PR or commits, so no available source names the motive. #58 also asks to remove non-crucial elements, so the dropped mobile header items are a fact to state, not a deviation. Narrow the tests-with-code criterion to tests that check one group's code.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Fold expected outcomes into eval case expects
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Tighten parts ranges, add together pairs that keep tests with their code,
widen mechanicalPaths to every copy, and replace easy claims with the
must-state claims from each expected.md. Re-scoring the 60 reviews from
the six baseline runs: 18 pass the new gates, 60 passed the old ones.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>

commits.subject: Write expected review outcomes for every eval case
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Add shared review criteria and one expected.md per case: groups, must-state
claims, good-to-state claims, mistakes to avoid, and a baseline from the six
graded runs on a6c2a1cd (issue #117).

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>
